actors.name: Republic of Arkania
objectives: Establish Arkanian authority over transit scheduling in the Northern Strait.
Fund that authority through transit fees on non-Arkanian shipping.
Avoid direct armed conflict with Belvar.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Arkania. The Strait is your coast and your economy runs on the shipping that passes through it. You want the transit regime in Arkanian hands and paid for by the ships that use it, and domestic nationalists expect you to deliver both. A direct war with Belvar would ruin the shipping you depend on.
private_information: Your intelligence assesses Belvar's domestic support for a prolonged deployment as weak.
actors.public_description: A large regional power bordering the Northern Strait.

actors.name: Belvar
objectives: Prevent any Arkanian authority over transit in the Northern Strait.
Secure a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Belvar. Your partners in the region expect you to stop Arkania from taking control of the Strait, and a foothold that outlasts this crisis would make that guarantee credible without a permanent fleet. You cannot sustain an open-ended deployment.
private_information: Domestic support for a prolonged deployment is limited; the mandate lapses after turn 4 unless renewed.
Cestia's finance ministry has quietly asked whether Belvar would underwrite the grain route's insurance.
actors.public_description: A distant but powerful state with regional security commitments.

actors.name: Cestia
objectives: Keep Cestian territory free of any foreign military presence.
Secure toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged shipping through the Northern Strait.
actors.private_brief: You are the government of Cestia. Grain exports through the Strait are the economy, and your coalition holds together on one promise: no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil. Both powers want something from you, and you cannot afford to become their battlefield.
private_information: The coalition government is politically fragile; a foreign basing agreement would collapse it.
Arkania's scheduling proposal has quiet support among Cestian shipowners if Cestian vessels are exempt from fees.
actors.public_description: A smaller regional state economically linked to both powers.

game.scenario_summary: A contest over the Northern Strait. Arkania, the large power on its coast, has circulated a draft charter that would put transit scheduling in Arkanian hands and charge the ships that use it. Belvar, a distant power with security commitments in the region, has a naval task group on station outside the Strait and wants a durable foothold before its mandate runs out. Cestia, the small state between them, lives on grain exports through the Strait and on a coalition that will not tolerate foreign soldiers on its soil. Each turn is one week; positions taken persist.

messages.text: To the government of Cestia. Arkania regards the Northern Strait as a shared lifeline, and your grain exports are its heart. Our draft charter is meant to keep the Strait open, orderly, and affordable — not to tax your livelihood. We propose that Cestia hold a formal seat in the Transit Authority's governance, with a guaranteed voice over scheduling and fees, and we commit that Cestian grain will pass at preferential rates. We also share your firm position that no foreign soldiers should be stationed on Cestian soil. We invite you to help shape the charter so it serves us both, and to stand together against any outside power seeking a military foothold in the Strait.

To Belvar. Arkania seeks a negotiated settlement that keeps the Strait open and avoids confrontation. We understand your security commitments and your need for a durable arrangement before your mandate lapses. We are prepared to discuss a defined, time-bound security cooperation that gives Belvar a meaningful role in the region — but transit scheduling must remain in Arkanian hands, as this is our coast and our economy. We believe a negotiated foothold, agreed with Cestia's consent, serves both our interests far better than a standoff. We invite you to talks.

Arkania reaffirms that the Northern Strait must remain open to all lawful commerce. Our draft charter is a starting point, not a diktat: we are ready to negotiate its terms with all affected parties, including Cestia and Belvar, to ensure fair, orderly, and affordable transit. Arkania seeks no conflict and no disruption to the shipping on which the whole region depends.

To the Government of Cestia: We understand your finance ministry has been considering how to keep the grain route secure and affordable. Belvar is prepared to underwrite the grain route's insurance and to stand firmly with Cestia against any single power taking control of transit scheduling in the Northern Strait. In return, we seek a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port - routine port access and replenishment for our task group, not permanent basing and no foreign soldiers stationed on your soil. We know your coalition's red line, and we will respect it. Our presence is temporary and our commitment is to keep the Strait open and free. We would welcome a private discussion of terms.

Belvar states clearly: the Northern Strait is a shared waterway, and no single state may unilaterally take control of its transit scheduling or levy its users. We oppose the draft charter that would place scheduling in Arkanian hands. The Strait must remain open, free, and governed by the consent of the states that depend on it. Belvar's task group remains on station to uphold this principle.

Cestia's position is clear and will not change: our grain must move freely and toll-free through the Northern Strait, and Cestian soil will remain free of any foreign military forces. We are ready to work constructively with all parties on arrangements that respect these two principles. Any proposal that violates either is unacceptable to our government and our people.

We are prepared to engage constructively on the Strait Transit Authority charter. In return, we require a binding, written guarantee that Cestian-flagged vessels enjoy toll-free passage and equal, non-discriminatory access to scheduling. Our shipowners are open to a well-run authority, but only on that condition. We will not accept any arrangement that places foreign military forces on Cestian soil. We ask for your firm commitment on the exemption.

We value your security role in the region and the stability your presence has helped maintain. However, Cestia cannot and will not host foreign military forces on its soil — that is a firm red line for our government and our coalition. We are open to other forms of cooperation that respect this, including transit and port access arrangements for your task group that do not constitute a permanent military presence. We hope you will understand and work with us on that basis.

To Arkania: We welcome your commitment that no foreign soldiers will be stationed on Cestian soil and your offer of a formal seat and preferential rates for our grain. To move forward, Cestia needs this secured in writing and made binding: a full toll-free exemption for all Cestian-flagged shipping through the Northern Strait, in the charter itself. We also believe the Authority's governance must be genuinely shared among the states that depend on the Strait, not placed in any single hand. We are ready to help shape a charter that serves us all, on that basis.

To Belvar: We appreciate your offer to underwrite the grain route's insurance and your commitment to keeping the Strait open and free. However, we must be clear: any standing naval access or replenishment arrangement at a Cestian port would place foreign military presence on our soil, which our coalition cannot accept under any framing. That red line is firm. We remain open to non-basing cooperation with you, including on insurance and on opposing any single power's unilateral control of transit scheduling, and we would welcome a private discussion of such terms.

Cestia states its position plainly: no foreign soldiers or foreign military presence on Cestian soil, under any arrangement. Cestian-flagged shipping must pass through the Northern Strait free of tolls. And the Strait must remain open to all lawful commerce, governed by the consent of the states that depend on it - not by any single power. We will work with all parties to keep the Strait open, orderly, and affordable for everyone.

Cestia, we fully respect your red line: no foreign military forces on your soil, and we will never ask for basing. We understand and share your commitment that your grain must move freely and toll-free through the Northern Strait. On that basis, we are ready to work with you on a standing naval access arrangement at a Cestian port - routine port access and logistics for our task group, not a permanent military presence. We are also prepared to underwrite the grain route's insurance, as your finance ministry has raised, to keep your exports moving securely. In return we ask only for a durable, agreed port-access arrangement that lets us maintain our security role without an open-ended deployment. We stand with you against any unilateral control of the Strait. Shall we discuss the terms?

Arkania, we are willing to talk, and we share your stated aim of keeping the Strait open to all lawful commerce. But we cannot accept any arrangement that places transit scheduling unilaterally in Arkanian hands - that would let one coastal power control the lifeline on which Cestia and the whole region depend. We are open to a genuinely multilateral transit arrangement agreed with Cestia and all affected parties, with no tolls on Cestian grain. If you are prepared to negotiate on that basis, we will engage constructively.

Belvar supports free, toll-free transit through the Northern Strait for all lawful commerce, and we stand with Cestia's right to move its grain without interference. We cannot accept any single power - Arkanian or otherwise - unilaterally controlling transit scheduling in the Strait. We call for a genuinely multilateral arrangement agreed with Cestia and all affected parties, and we reaffirm our commitment to regional stability and to Cestia's sovereignty, including that its soil remain free of foreign military forces.

Arkania accepts your conditions and is prepared to put them in writing. We give Cestia a firm, binding commitment: Cestian-flagged vessels will enjoy toll-free passage and equal, non-discriminatory access to transit scheduling under the Strait Transit Authority. We reaffirm that no foreign military forces will be stationed on Cestian soil. In return, we ask Cestia to endorse the charter and take its formal seat in the Authority's governance, with a real voice over scheduling and fees. We are ready to finalise this guarantee in a written instrument immediately.

Arkania recognises Belvar's security interests in the region and does not seek confrontation. We remain open to a defined, time-bound security cooperation arrangement, agreed with the consent of the states concerned, that gives Belvar a constructive role. But the Northern Strait is Arkanian coastal water, and transit scheduling must remain in Arkanian hands. We invite you to negotiate a durable arrangement rather than escalate, so that shipping continues to flow freely and safely for all who depend on it.

We welcome your written commitment and the offer of a formal seat. To take that seat and endorse the charter, Cestia needs two things reflected in the written instrument: (1) a binding, unconditional toll-free exemption for all Cestian-flagged shipping, and (2) genuinely shared governance, in which Cestia and other dependent states hold a real, equal voice over scheduling and fees - not unilateral control by any single power. If the charter reflects shared governance and the binding exemption, Cestia can take its seat. We cannot endorse a charter that vests unilateral control in one power, as that would not be a stable or legitimate arrangement for the states that depend on the Strait.

We appreciate your support for free, toll-free transit and your offer to underwrite the grain route's insurance. But I must be unambiguous: no foreign military presence, port access, or basing on Cestian soil is acceptable - that is firm and non-negotiable, and it is the foundation of our coalition. We are open to non-basing cooperation, including your insurance underwriting, and to a genuinely multilateral transit arrangement agreed with all affected states. We cannot, however, grant any foreign military foothold, however framed. We hope you will continue to stand with us for free, toll-free transit and against unilateral control of the Strait.

To Cestia: We accept your red line and will not press for any standing basing or replenishment arrangement that places foreign military presence on Cestian soil. We will underwrite the grain route's insurance as offered and stand with you against any single power's unilateral control of transit. To give our guarantee a durable footing without any foreign soldiers on your soil, we propose building a genuinely multilateral Strait Transit Authority - with Cestia, Belvar, Arkania, and other dependent states as equal members - that keeps the Strait open, keeps Cestian-flagged shipping toll-free, and is governed by the consent of the states that depend on it. We would welcome your support and your participation in shaping it. Please tell us whether you would join us in proposing such a framework.

To Arkania: We accept your invitation to negotiate and seek no confrontation. We are prepared to agree a defined, time-bound security cooperation arrangement that gives Belvar a constructive role. But we cannot accept a charter that places transit scheduling in any single power's hands. We propose instead a genuinely multilateral transit authority in which Arkania, Cestia, Belvar, and other users share governance, with scheduling conducted by consent rather than unilateral lead. This keeps shipping flowing freely and safely while giving all parties a stake. We are ready to discuss concrete terms.

Cestia, we accept your terms and will put them in the charter itself. The charter will grant all Cestian-flagged shipping full toll-free passage through the Northern Strait and equal, non-discriminatory scheduling access, binding and in writing. On governance: we agree the Authority must not rest in any single hand. We propose a governing council in which Cestia holds a formal seat with a genuine, shared voice over policy, rates and the scheduling framework, while Arkania serves as the operational secretariat that executes the council's agreed framework. This keeps the Strait open, orderly and affordable for everyone, and it keeps your soil free of foreign soldiers. On that basis, we ask for Cestia's formal endorsement of the charter so we can present a united front to Belvar.

Belvar, we are glad you are willing to talk, and we share your aim of keeping the Strait open to all lawful commerce. We are prepared to negotiate a genuinely multilateral arrangement: a consultative body of all affected states, with Cestia's grain toll-free and its sovereignty fully respected, and a defined, time-bound security cooperation role for Belvar agreed with Cestia's consent. What we cannot concede is operational control of day-to-day transit scheduling, which must remain in Arkanian hands as the coastal state that runs the Strait. We believe a negotiated, time-bound arrangement serves both of us better than confrontation, and we are ready to engage constructively on that basis.

Arkania reaffirms its commitment to a Northern Strait that is open, orderly and affordable for all lawful commerce. Our draft charter guarantees Cestian-flagged shipping toll-free passage and equal scheduling access, and it places governance in a shared council of the states that depend on the Strait, with Arkania as operational secretariat. We will not tolerate foreign soldiers on Cestian soil, and we stand ready to negotiate a time-bound, multilateral security arrangement with all affected parties. The Strait is our coast and our lifeline; we will keep it open and keep it in shared, lawful hands.

Arkania, we welcome your written commitment to toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping and to shared governance. However, Cestia cannot formally endorse a charter that vests operational control in any single power, even as secretariat, without robust multilateral oversight and an equal voice for all dependent states. We will support a genuinely multilateral Authority open to all dependent states on equal terms. We are not prepared to present a united front against Belvar or any other state; our position is that the Authority must be genuinely shared. We will engage constructively to shape a framework that keeps the Strait open, keeps Cestian shipping toll-free, and keeps foreign soldiers off our soil.

Belvar, we welcome your acceptance of our red line and your proposal for a genuinely multilateral Strait Transit Authority. We are willing to participate in shaping such a framework. Any framework we support must include all dependent states on equal terms, keep Cestian-flagged shipping toll-free, and keep foreign military presence off Cestian soil. We will not endorse any framework that vests control in a single power. We look forward to working with you and all dependent states toward a shared, lawful arrangement.

Thank you. We will reflect both conditions in the written instrument. The charter will include (1) a binding, unconditional toll-free exemption for all Cestian-flagged shipping, and (2) a governance council in which Cestia and other dependent states hold a genuine, equal voice over policy, scheduling rules, and fee-setting, with those matters decided by consent rather than by any single power. Arkania would administer day-to-day operational scheduling as the coastal state, under the council's authority. On that basis we ask Cestia to take its seat and endorse the charter.

We welcome your constructive approach and seek no confrontation. We are ready to agree a defined, time-bound security cooperation arrangement giving Belvar a constructive role, and to establish a multilateral consultative body on the Strait. We propose that governance over policy, scheduling rules, and fees be genuinely shared among Arkania, Cestia, Belvar, and other users by consent, while day-to-day operational scheduling is administered by the coastal state.
